ZISTSHAHR / BEYOND THE IMAGE

THE WORK BEHIND THE VISION

Not just a city.
A different idea of living.

Zistshahr is a research-led proposal connecting urban form, social relations, open science, independent small-scale production, ecology and the systems that sustain everyday life. This visual journey illustrates concepts; it is not a claim that a physical city has already been built.

Walk through the productive house, the neighborhood, shared livelihood, collective infrastructure and regenerative cycles.

II

The foundations

Discover the theoretical inquiry: human agency, competing theories of social order, and the connection between values and urban form.

02 / THE OPEN-SCIENCE PRINCIPLE — PROJECT CATALOGUE

Knowledge should
multiply agency.

In the project’s normative proposal, open science means both designing technologies that smaller, independent producers can actually use, and sharing the resulting know-how. Free information alone cannot overcome a technology's capital-intensive design.

01Begin with lived needsResearch questions arise from households and everyday production.
02Build usable toolsDesign for accessible scales of production, not only large industry.
03Open the knowledgeMake discoveries available for adaptation and replication.
04Share the benefitsEnable community-funded R&D to serve beyond its funders.
PROVENANCE The open-science principles are adapted from the project-provided Persian catalogue “دانش آزاد”. These are proposed goals, not evidence of achieved outcomes. The accompanying presentation “Beyond-Market Science” discusses value creation, innovation and public investment, including Mariana Mazzucato’s work.

03 / THEORETICAL FOUNDATIONSTHE FOUR-MODEL TYPOLOGY / FROM THE SUPPLIED RESEARCH
THE FIRST QUESTION IS NEVER HOW TO BUILD.

Before the form,
the human vision.

Zistshahr asks a foundational question: which social relations should a city make possible? The comparison below is a proposed interpretive framework developed in the project's research materials—not a universal or exhaustive classification of societies.

DIMENSIONDOMINATIONMARKETANARCHIST SOCIETYPROPHETIC UMMAH
Primary motivationSelf-interest in powerSelf-regarding pursuit of gainCommon-interest cooperationOther-regarding care and affection
Mechanism of orderFear of ruling powerFree competitionCooperationHuman dignity
Roles and responsibilityCapacity to exercise powerCapacity to generate wealthSmall assemblies and councilsCapacity for service and conscious self-sacrifice
01 / HOBBES · 1651

“Covenants, without the Sword, are but Words.”

Leviathan, XVII. A reference point for a theory of order mediated by sovereign power, not a complete description of Hobbes.
02 / ADAM SMITH · 1776

“Led by an invisible hand to promote an end...”

The Wealth of Nations, IV.ii. A point of departure for thinking about decentralized exchange and unintended social outcomes.
03 / IMMANUEL KANT · 1784

“The unsocial sociality of man.”

Idea for a Universal History, Proposition IV. The tension between sociability and antagonism is a problem for social design.

Values → institutions → space → everyday possibilities.

OPEN KNOWLEDGE / PEOPLE-LED RESEARCH

Knowledge beyond the market

Open up the means of making. Give more people the tools to shape their own livelihoods.

01

When production concentrates

As production becomes more capital intensive and concentrated, independent livelihoods become harder to sustain. Zistshahr asks how technology could widen access to productive work.

02

When know-how is enclosed

Patents and exclusive licensing can limit independent producers’ access to technical knowledge. Dependence can extend from machinery to the know-how needed to use it.

03

Two missions for research

Develop technology that people can use at an accessible scale, and publish the resulting knowledge openly so others can adapt and improve it.

04

Multiply productive capacity

One path grows output through larger firms and concentrated capital. The project’s alternative multiplies the ability to produce across homes, workshops and independent units.

05

From people, for everyone

Start with needs people identify. Bring local ingenuity together with specialist knowledge, then make the results available for adaptation and reuse around the world.

06

Livelihoods with more freedom

The aim is to reduce dependence on capital owners for a livelihood and give people more room for creativity and initiative. Capital and technology serve human development.

07 / From principle to prototype

Zistshahr reports establishing an endowment-backed R&D centre for technology suitable for independent producers. The stages below come from the project team’s account.

LABORATORY STAGE

Stirling engine

A closed-cycle heat engine converts a temperature difference into motion and can drive an alternator. The design uses readily available parts and aims to be buildable in a small workshop with introductory training.

LAB DEMONSTRATION · PROTOTYPE FUNDING

Small-scale LNG

The team reports demonstrating liquefaction in the lab with comparatively simple equipment. Funding for a commercial prototype is being sought.

TWO METALS DEMONSTRATED · PILOT FUNDING

Small-scale mineral processing

The team reports validation for two metals and successful tests involving six metals and their compounds. The process targets low waste and workshop-scale extraction, including potential use for interstitial deposits and rare earths. Funding for a production line is being sought.

CONCEPT OUTREACH

Micro-refinery

Smaller-scale refining could lower the capital needed to enter parts of the energy sector. The project is introducing the concept and inviting discussion.
